card.name: Just before an old-fashioned first name
card.fires_on: The word or mark right before a person's first name in historical or biographical text, such as a title, "Mr.", "Mrs.", a comma, "and" or "by". It marks the spot where a first name like Harry, Arthur or Herbert could come next.

modes.label: After a title
modes.description: A title or honorific such as Mr., Mrs. or Umpire comes just before a name.
modes.example: Bridgeport Parks Commissioner, Mr<<.>> Wesley Hayes, began a campaign

modes.label: Linking words before a person
modes.description: A comma, "and", "by" or "was" comes just before a named person in a list or an attribution.
modes.example: Stan Coveleski<< and>> Sam Jones to their first minor league contracts

card.writes: It pushes the model toward older, traditional male first names such as Harry, Herbert and Arthur, and away from modern ones such as Chris and Jeremy.
card.plain: It fires just before a person's first name in old historical writing and favors old-fashioned male names.
